HEADLINE: Farage: Burnham reopening Brexit debate is gift for Reform
Sub: Brexiteer says Labour's suggestion of rejoining the EU might give him biggest 'ever' boost in his career
Photo caption: Nigel Farage said a referendum on rejoining the EU would 'bitterly' divide the country. Credit: Christopher Furlong/Getty

Nigel Farage has said Andy Burnham has given him a "gift" in reopening the Brexit debate.
The Reform UK leader said a referendum on rejoining the EU would "bitterly" divide the country, and accused the Prime Minister of contradicting his own plans for devolution.
It comes after Mr Burnham said a second Brexit referendum was a possibility as part of his review of Britain's relationship with the EU.
After addressing an auditorium of Reform supporters in Doncaster on Thursday, Mr Farage told The Telegraph: "Andy Burnham has given me the biggest gift of my career.
"If he wants to fight the next election in the Red Wall on rejoining the European Union, then bring it on."
Mr Burnham told broadcasters on Wednesday that it was "possible" that Labour's next election manifesto could include a pledge to hold an in-out referendum on the EU, or to rejoin the bloc without another vote.
The Prime Minister has said the UK's position in Europe "isn't good enough" and that he would consider a "whole range of options" including rejoining the EU, returning to the customs union and a Canada-style "associate membership".
He told Labour members in his conference speech on Tuesday that Brexit had "done more harm than good" and promised to set out options for the country's future relationship around the time of the next summit with Brussels in November.
